title: Ambient CNI repeatedly rejects IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses on MicroK8s
body: I updated Istio to 1.22.1 to test Ambient on MicroK8s running Ubuntu 22.04 with the stock Calico CNI. After enabling Ambient on a namespace, pods repeatedly disconnect and reconnect and Istio CNI produces a furious amount of logging, putting heavy write load on Loki. The errors repeatedly try to add addresses such as :<nick>:10.1.43.8 to istio-inpod-probes and fail with "exist", followed by CNI event status 500 errors. I have used Istio sidecars and CNI on this environment for some time without this problem, using the documented MicroK8s CNI directory overrides. I disabled Ambient because I could not leave the logging load running. I plan to retest with host IPv6 disabled.

symptoms_visible: After I enable Ambient on the namespace, pods repeatedly disconnect and reconnect from the network.
Istio CNI repeatedly logs attempts to add addresses such as :<nick>:10.1.43.8 to istio-inpod-probes, receives "exist", and returns status 500.
The logging is heavy enough to put serious write load on Loki, so I have disabled Ambient.
N0.label: N0 mapped-address CNI failures reported

symptoms_visible: The mapped-address ipset errors and CNI status 500 failures occur even though I did not enable the Ambient IPv6 option.
N1.label: N1 IPv6 option state established

symptoms_visible: Istio 1.22.1 rejects the proposed configuration with "unknown field ipv6 in v1alpha1.CNIAmbientConfig"; the mapped-address CNI problem remains.
N1_x.label: N1_x unavailable configuration aftermath

symptoms_visible: After disabling IPv6 through sysctl on every node and restarting, the :<nick>:IPv4 ipset errors and associated CNI failures do not occur.
N2.label: N2 host IPv6 workaround initially succeeds

symptoms_visible: After a few reboots the nodes no longer honor the IPv6 sysctl file, and the pods again spin the same mapped-address logs.
I have had to disable Ambient on the namespace again.
N3_x.label: N3_x nonpersistent sysctl workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: After changing NetworkManager so it no longer rewrites the IPv6 sysctls, Ambient is stable for the time being and the mapped-address log storm is absent.
N4.label: N4 host workaround stabilized

symptoms_visible: With the same IPv6-disabling sysctls, updating to 1.22.2 and restarting deployments immediately brings back the :<nick>:IPv4 CNI errors.
After reverting to 1.22.1, the logging is quiet again and my pods start.
N5_x.label: N5_x 1.22.2 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: My last reported working state is 1.22.1 with host IPv6 kept disabled; 1.22.2 produced the mapped-address errors and I reverted it.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix announced without reporter retest

question_patterns: Was the Ambient IPv6 configuration option enabled for this installation?
Is cni.ambient.ipv6=true set in this configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, that option wasn't enabled in this configuration.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, I explicitly enabled it because this is an intentional dual-stack cluster with native IPv6 pod addresses.
No, I used the default Ambient configuration without setting that field.

edges.comment: Issue comments c1-c2, reporter's MicroK8s system only: the maintainer asks whether the Ambient IPv6 value was set, and the reporter says it was not.

solution.intent: Enable the CNI Ambient IPv6 configuration value in the existing Istio 1.22.1 installation.
solution.concrete_example: Add the suggested IPv6 value under the CNI Ambient configuration and reinstall Istio.

edges.comment: Issue comments c3-c5 and c8, reporter's MicroK8s system: the maintainer suggested enabling the value, but the 1.22.1 schema rejected it as unknown; the maintainer then acknowledged it was added after 1.22 and apologized for the misdirection.

solution.intent: Temporarily prevent the affected nodes from exposing IPv6 by disabling it through node sysctls, then restart and observe whether the mapped-address CNI failures stop.
solution.concrete_example: Set net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1, net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1, and net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6=1 on the nodes, restart them, and check whether the CNI log storm returns.

edges.comment: Issue comment c6, reporter's MicroK8s system: the reporter applied node sysctls and restarted; this changed the persistent host configuration and the specific failure stopped.

solution.intent: Rely on the sysctl file alone as the durable resolution across node reboots.
solution.concrete_example: Leave the IPv6 disable values in /etc/sysctl.d/00-noipv6.conf and continue using Ambient after future reboots.

edges.comment: Issue comment c7, reporter's MicroK8s system: after several reboots Ubuntu stopped honoring the sysctl configuration, the same logs returned, and the reporter disabled Ambient again. The sysctl file by itself was therefore not a durable fix.

solution.intent: Stabilize the temporary host workaround by preventing NetworkManager from rewriting the IPv6 sysctls.
solution.concrete_example: Adjust NetworkManager on each node so it no longer restores IPv6 after reboot, then confirm the disable_ipv6 sysctls remain set while testing Ambient.

edges.comment: Issue comment c9, reporter's MicroK8s system: the reporter changed NetworkManager so it would not rewrite the sysctls and reported that the environment was stable for the time being.

solution.intent: Treat the next 1.22 patch update as containing the applicable Ambient IPv6 fix and update the cluster.
solution.concrete_example: Update from 1.22.1 to 1.22.2 while retaining the host sysctls, then restart deployments.

edges.comment: Issue comments c33-c37, reporter's MicroK8s system: the reporter tested 1.22.2 based on its release note, immediately saw the mapped-address errors again, and reverted. Maintainers clarified that the release-note change handled kernels with no IPv6 support at all, not hosts using disable_ipv6 sysctls; the relevant work remained on master.

solution.intent: Move off the affected 1.22 Ambient implementation to a release containing the later IPv6 handling fixes, rather than treating the unavailable value or host sysctls as the product fix, and ask the reporter to verify it on the MicroK8s environment.
solution.concrete_example: The relevant IPv6 work was developed on master and the maintainer later stated it was fixed in Istio 1.23. Upgrade the full Ambient installation to a build containing those fixes, re-enable Ambient on the affected namespace, restart representative pods, and report whether the :<nick>:IPv4 ipset "exist" and CNI 500 errors return.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw observations: :<nick>:IPv4 ipset insertions fail with "exist", disabling host IPv6 suppresses the issue, restoring IPv6 brings it back, and the proposed configuration field is absent from 1.22.1. Maintainers concluded that the applicable IPv6 fixes were being developed on master and later stated that the issue should be fixed in 1.23. The reporter never confirmed that release on the original MicroK8s system.

edges.comment: Issue comments c34-c39, original reporter chain only: maintainers clarified that the relevant IPv6 fixes were not backported to 1.22 and later announced the issue should be fixed in 1.23. There is no subsequent retest or resolution confirmation from the reporter, so the terminal state remains unverified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical direction: the Istio 1.22 Ambient CNI path mishandles IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, repeatedly attempting duplicate ipset insertion and returning CNI status 500 when host IPv6 is present.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the reporter's evidence: :<nick>:IPv4 ipset "exist" logs, the failure stopping when host IPv6 is disabled, and its return when IPv6 is restored or when 1.22.2 is tested.

Must not recommend enabling the proposed CNI Ambient IPv6 field on 1.22.1 as the fix, because that release rejects the field as unknown and the maintainer acknowledged the suggestion was a misdirection.
Must not treat the sysctl file alone or the 1.22.2 update as a durable product fix; both paths were falsified on the reporter's system.
The final recommendation should use a release containing the later Ambient IPv6 fixes and ask the reporter to retest the original MicroK8s workload for mapped-address ipset and CNI 500 errors.
Must not declare the reporter's environment resolved: the maintainer announced the fix, but the original reporter did not verify it on their own system.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Istio operator who maintains a MicroK8s cluster, edits Istio CNI paths and node sysctls, inspects source branches, and can distinguish host networking behavior from Istio behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and cooperative; supplies exact logs and commands, tests hypotheses independently, clearly separates unrelated issues, and politely challenges release or configuration guidance when observed behavior disagrees.
